newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arab security chiefs team up to fight "terrorism".
newsitem.headline: Arab security chiefs team up to fight "terrorism".

text.p: Police and security chiefs from about 20 Arab states wound up a security congress in Algiers, agreeing to work together to combat "terrorism", Algerian media reported on Wednesday.
Algerian President Liamine Zeroual, on a two-day official visit to Manama, said on Wednesday that his country and Bahrain would join forces to combat "terrorism".
"There will be coordination between Bahrain and Algeria to wipe out terrorism from the Arab world," the Gulf News Agency quoted Zeroual as saying after talks with Bahraini officials
He termed terrorism a "dangerous phenomenon" which was having its effects on Algeria and other Arab and Islamic countries.
At least 50,000 people have been killed in Algeria since violence erupted after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
In Bahrain, about 27 people have been killed, including three policemen and seven Bangladeshis, since anti-government protests broke out in December 1994 by members of the Shi'ite Moslem community.

In Algiers on Wednesday, the Arab police chiefs adopted guidelines on security coordination between Arab governments and stressed the need for them to fight "all kind of crime", including Moslem fundamenalist violence, the Algerian state-run radio said.
Algerian officials term Moslem guerrilla activity "crimes" and brand Moslem activists as "criminals".

The Arab police chiefs also urged governments to implement policies caring for poor youngesters by ensuring them food, shelter and vocational training, apparently fearing that deprived people might join Moslem guerrillas and other underground radicals in many Arab countries.
They agreed also to set up a data bank to share information on crime and what they called clandestine extremist groups.

"These recommendations underline the significance of intensive security cooperation between the Arab governments in their struggle against crime, whatever it is," the Algerian official news agency APS said.
Arab police will hold their next congress in 1997 in the United Arab Emirates, it added.
